transcript:

Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
Airlines across the U.S. are facing a backlog of canceled flights this morning following an hours-long ground stop on Friday.
The Department of Transportation says restoring normal operations will take time.
More than 3,000 planes were in the air when the FAA reported instability in its radar and communication system.
NPR's Deepa Shivaram reports.
Department of Homeland Security Secretary Mark Wayne Mullen briefed reporters at the White House after the ground stop was lifted.
The public was never at danger through this process.
There was never any lives at risk.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy also briefed reporters.
He says the FAA switches got overloaded with data, became inconsistent, and because of that, they shut the system down.
The secretary says Congress needs to fund a package that would help the FAA with new technology.
In the meantime, Duffy says a ground stop like this could happen again with the old technology in place.
Deepa Shivaram, NPR News, the White House.
Nearly 200 countries meeting at a climate summit in Turkey are negotiating how to cut fossil fuel emissions as the world falls short of its climate goals.
NPR's Lauren Summer reports on what they're hoping to achieve before talks wrap up next week.
It was 11 years ago now that countries agreed on a goal to stave off the most intense impacts of climate change.
Warming would be limited to 1.5 degrees Celsius, which is 2.7 degrees Fahrenheit.
Now that goal is out of reach.
The planet has almost reached that level of warming, and countries continue to burn fossil fuels.
Discussions at the COP 31 climate summit are now focused on how much hotter it will get, which affects extreme weather around the planet.
Despite the U.S. being one of the largest producers of greenhouse gas emissions, the Trump administration is not participating in the talks.
Lauren Summer, NPR News.
Investigators are working to determine why a tanker struck a docked cruise boat in New Orleans on Friday.
NPR's Debbie Elliott reports more than 30 people were taken to area hospitals with injuries.
The tanker, called Atlantic Asphalt, struck the American Heritage paddle wheeler just after noon as passengers were disembarking.
The impact quickly toppled and sank the cruise ship, sending people into the water.
New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno says police, firefighters, the Coast Guard, and nearby ships came to the rescue.
We have zero people unaccounted for, which truly is a miracle on the Mississippi.
Video shows the tanker appearing to lose steerage after it navigated a sharp crescent turn in the Mississippi River at New Orleans.
The crash closed down river traffic for much of the day. Debbie Elliott, NPR News.
This is NPR News in Washington.
Microsoft says service is fully restored following a global outage that disrupted outlook, teams, and its A.I. assistant co-pilot for hours this week.
The company says the underlying problem has been fixed and the outage was not related to a cyber attack.
Scientists have created a map of the part of the brain implicated in diseases like schizophrenia and Alzheimer's.
NPR's Ping Huang reports.
The basal ganglia are a set of interconnected brain structures tucked beneath the cerebral cortex.
Hong Kui Zen, director of brain science at the Allen Institute, says they're key to some important brain functions.
Including movement control, decision making, habit formation, as well as reward and emotion.
They're also key to some psychiatric disorders and diseases that affect the nervous system.
So over three years, with funding from the National Institutes of Health, she and colleagues at more than 50 research institutions
came together to create a cellular atlas of the different cell types and the basal ganglia across humans and primates.
The results are out in more than two dozen papers published by Cell Press.
The next step, she says, is to map the whole brain.
Ping Huang, NPR News.
Canada and the U.S. are making progress toward a trade deal. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney says he spoke with President Trump
and senior officials ahead of a regional summit in the Philippines next week.
Canada is seeking to reduce its reliance on U.S. trade following the collapse of negotiations in August.
I'm Windsor Johnston, NPR News, in Washington.

Nearly 200 countries negotiate fossil fuel emission cuts at climate summit in Turkey as goals slip
